findings.message: src/integrations/inbound_api.py:209-217 (EP-02 GET /v1/cases/{case_id}/status) returns the raw result of CaseStore().read_case(case_id). It does not apply masking. The host's own case route (src/solution/case_routes.py:36) wraps the same read in solution.masking.mask_fields. INT_01's policy says to mask the full mobile number and PAN. Because no auth is checked (recorded gap), this endpoint gives full PAN, Aadhaar and mobile values to any caller. Apply mask_fields before returning, as the host already does.

src/integrations/inbound_api.py:194-206: submit_case calls store.create_case(case_id) before it awaits enter_case(). If enter_case raises (model residency refusal, an agent error, a DB error), the case row stays but no entry is stored. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key then hits the 'existing case' branch and returns status 'received' without running anything. The case is silently lost, and the declared 5xx action ('Retry ×3, then degrade to human') can never happen. Treat a case without a stored entry as not yet entered, or handle the enter_case failure explicitly.

src/agents/blk_01.py:393-405: enforce_br_act_01 refuses a duplicate mobile number only when the caller passes registered_mobile_numbers or the TOOL_01 response carries duplicate=True. act_01 (line 462-470) passes neither, and the TOOL_01 stub never sets the flag. In practice 'Mobile number unique' therefore always passes. This is the adverse case of a blocking rule that the harness runs, and tacit knowledge TK-01 says users bypass this exact check. The recorded gaps cover only the email format, pincode and IFSC parameters, not the missing uniqueness source (INT_DB1 is not configured). Record it as a gap, or refuse when uniqueness cannot be proven, rather than letting the check pass silently.

src/agents/blk_01.py:304-309 invents EMAIL_PATTERN, PINCODE_PATTERN (six digits, not starting with 0) and IFSC_PATTERN (RBI format) for BR-ACT_01, BR-ACT_03 and BR-ACT_04. The Precord gives no value for any of them. The register says: 'Do not guess the value.' This is recorded as a gap, so it is a known gap, but blocking enforcers in the write set still refuse cases on values the Precord never stated. Contrast blk_02.py:116-117, which correctly leaves PERMITTED_EXTENSIONS and MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES undeclared.

src/agents/blk_01.py:417-425 and 482-486: enforce_br_act_03 compares Pincode with 'State', but act_03 passes only _reads(case, 'ACT_03'). That set does not include State (ACT_03 reads Name, Gender, Date of Birth, Address, Pincode), and PINCODE_STATE_REFERENCE is empty. The 'Pincode and state match' branch is dead code. It is a known gap, but the enforcer suggests a check it can never perform.

src/agents/blk_01_2.py:399-410: the registered tool_01 callable takes correlation_id as a parameter of the ADK function tool. ADK exposes it in the tool schema, so the model fills it in (or it defaults to ''), and invoke() gets a correlation ID made up by the model instead of the case ID. blk_01_1.py:346-348 and blk_02.py:419-422 correctly read it from ToolContext.state. Read it from tool_context here too.

src/agents/blk_02.py:462-477 and 598-606: when ACT_07 finds any missing slot, it raises QCDiscrepancyDetected. run_case then routes to EXC_05 and returns the unchanged input case. Neither 'Reviewer remark drafts' nor 'Discrepancy recommendation list' (ACT_07's declared writes) reaches the case, and the case never reaches CHK_02, which the Precord routes ACT_07's draft to. The Precord's EXC_05 detection is 'Confidence score below threshold', and that threshold is undeclared. Turning every discrepancy into an exception bypasses the required reviewer checkpoint and drops the draft that the reviewer is supposed to inspect.

src/agents/blk_01.py:634-635 returns next=details['on_failure'] (an exception ID) on a routed case. The contract says next is the on_success of the last action, or None, and blk_02 returns None. Separately, src/agents/blk_02.py:585 appends action_id to trace before the action runs, so a failed action appears in the 'actions that ran'. blk_01 appends only after success. Align both with the declared run_case shape.

The recorded verifier results show A11 (hand-written loop) failing for all four agent modules, C3-8 (arithmetic) failing for blk_01.py:511 and blk_01_2.py:238, and C3-7 unverified for BLK_01 and BLK_02. The flagged loops are the declared action chain and blk_02.py:528, which is the INT_02 channel fallback loop, not a retry. The flagged arithmetic is a mask length (len-4) and a set difference. These look like checker false positives, but they are still open conformance gaps. Per the register they block promotion until each is fixed or recorded as a deviation. blk_01.py:510-511 could drop its own fallback and rely only on solution.masking.mask_value.

src/agents/blk_01.py:267-278 gives GR-01..GR-04 messages of the form 'GR-0n refuses: …'. spec/rules.csv declares an empty message for the guardrail rows. Use the rule text, as blk_02.py:155-158 does, or leave the message empty. Do not invent message text.

agent_version is owed from MVP and the rung is Pilot. blk_01.py:172 correctly sets AGENT_VERSION = '', but blk_02.py:276 ('BLK_02@'+PRECORD[:12]), blk_01_1.py:50 ('BLK_01.1@1') and blk_01_2.py:184-186 (a computed hash) emit invented version values. blk_01_2.py:311,314 also defaults event confidence to 1.0 and guardrail_event to 'none', while the other modules use 0.0 and ''. That makes calibration data (KPI_O9) look like full confidence without any being measured.

src/agents/blk_01_2.py:62 assumes SERVES_STEPS = S1–S4 (the parent's), so allowed_step returns True for intake and KYC steps that are not part of Bank Details Validation. src/agents/blk_01_1.py:77 makes the opposite choice (empty). Both are assumptions about a field agents.yaml leaves blank (recorded as gaps), but the two sibling sub-agents treat the same gap in opposite ways. Pick one rule and record it once.

src/agents/blk_02.py:210-216 still embeds prompt text that tells the model it serves 'S5, S6, and S7' and should 'Generate declaration PDF support'. SCOPE_NOTE (line 250-258) overrides this, and allowed_step and GR-02 refuse S6 in code, so S6 is not automated. The S6 claim is a Precord conflict (ownership lists S6 for both BLK_02 and a person; HR-107 was dismissed). It should be carried as a deviation row for Module 1, not only as a prompt override.

src/integrations/inbound_api.py:279-282: when the stored record's checkpoint_id is not CHK_01 or CHK_02, allowed is None and any action string is passed to store.apply. Offer exactly decisions[].action: refuse a decision for a checkpoint the Precord does not declare. reviewer_role is also not checked against the checkpoint's role; that may belong to C5.
